hypotheses.title: Selective learned memory access
hypotheses.mechanism: An original learned controller selects and updates external state rather than processing all stored experience on each query.
hypotheses.prediction: Under matched information and measured training/inference budgets, the candidate improves retention at increasing delay and capacity while preserving held-out task accuracy.
hypotheses.falsifier: The advantage disappears with credible learned baselines, access-cost accounting, memory ablation, or held-out operation structures.

hypotheses.title: Adaptive recurrent computation
hypotheses.mechanism: Shared learned computation selects additional iterations or halts based on state and uncertainty signals.
hypotheses.prediction: A learned allocation rule improves the quality/cost frontier relative to fixed-depth and fixed-budget controls after charging routing and halting overhead.
hypotheses.falsifier: The apparent benefit is explained by greater total compute, favorable example selection, uncharged routing, or failure on unfamiliar compositions.

hypotheses.title: Learned reusable computation
hypotheses.mechanism: Repeated task structure becomes reusable learned computation without requiring a predefined human cognitive taxonomy.
hypotheses.prediction: New bindings and held-out compositions reuse acquired structure with lower total cost than equivalent retraining or repeated search, including acquisition and verification cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reuse reduces to answer memorization, relies on an undisclosed runtime solver or unequal task-specific supervision, fails compositional transfer, or costs more overall than the matched control.

hypotheses.title: Continual adaptation with bounded interference
hypotheses.mechanism: Separately measured state writes and learned-parameter changes preserve plasticity while constraining interference and growth.
hypotheses.prediction: The candidate learns sequential tasks while retaining earlier competence under a fixed total memory and adaptation budget.
hypotheses.falsifier: Retention comes from unbounded storage/replay, adaptation stalls, or improvements disappear under equal replay and update budgets.

hypotheses.title: Reversible acquisition before persistent promotion
hypotheses.mechanism: New learned state or reusable computation is first versioned in a bounded working area; a learned selection rule proposes promotion and permits invalidation.
hypotheses.prediction: At equal total resource cost, staged acquisition improves recovery from misleading updates without materially reducing useful adaptation or unseen-task transfer.
hypotheses.falsifier: Promotion and checking overhead dominate, error recovery requires oracle labels unavailable to controls, or the candidate only succeeds with hand-coded semantic categories.

hypotheses.title: Units of cognition beyond tokens
hypotheses.question: Does cognition need tokens as its fundamental unit?
hypotheses.mechanism: An own-initialized system may learn internal units whose boundaries are not inherited from language tokenization.
hypotheses.prediction: A registered future comparison could find representations that preserve task information and transfer while reducing total conversion and computation cost against token-based controls.
hypotheses.falsifier: The alternative loses necessary information, fails transfer, or its advantage disappears after charging representation learning, conversion, and execution.

hypotheses.title: Multiple native representations
hypotheses.question: Can different information classes have different native representations?
hypotheses.mechanism: The system may select or acquire heterogeneous representations without requiring a single universal serialization for cognition.
hypotheses.prediction: A registered future comparison could show useful transfer across native formats with less total work than forcing every input through a single representation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Benefits require task-specific hand routing, incompatible isolated experts, or uncharged conversions and do not survive unseen input combinations.

hypotheses.title: Discovered intermediate computation
hypotheses.question: Can the system discover its own intermediate computational representation?
hypotheses.mechanism: Learning may shape intermediate structures and permissible transformations instead of operating only inside a designer-fixed cognitive language.
hypotheses.prediction: A registered future comparison could show acquired intermediate structure that transfers across tasks and bindings after charging discovery and execution costs.
hypotheses.falsifier: The structure is a renamed fixed instruction inventory, a task identifier, or a memorized solution and does not support held-out composition.

hypotheses.title: Temporary executable structures
hypotheses.question: Can learned computation construct temporary executable structures?
hypotheses.mechanism: A learned planner may assemble bounded transient work structures whose execution changes with the problem, rather than only selecting fixed-depth transformations.
hypotheses.prediction: A registered future comparison could demonstrate useful unseen compositions at lower total cost than matched static or search controls, including construction and checking.
hypotheses.falsifier: Only scripted graph construction works, learned proposals need an oracle, or gains disappear when invalid proposals and construction costs are included.

hypotheses.title: Transfer without a compulsory text bottleneck
hypotheses.question: Can information move between linguistic, relational, spatial, mathematical, procedural, causal, and perceptual representations without everything becoming text?
hypotheses.mechanism: Learned transformations may preserve task-relevant relationships between native representations; these examples are not a required human category inventory.
hypotheses.prediction: A registered future comparison could preserve cross-representation constraints and transfer to unseen combinations without a mandatory language serialization step.
hypotheses.falsifier: Transfers discard required structure, rely on pretrained translators or hand-coded semantic solutions, or fail when wording and modality correlations change.

hypotheses.title: Learning how to represent a problem
hypotheses.question: Can the system learn how to represent a problem, rather than merely how to solve a problem once represented?
hypotheses.mechanism: Learning may change the problem representation itself through downstream or predictive objectives under a bounded acquisition budget with explicit supplied structure and supervision.
hypotheses.prediction: On tasks with adequate learned acquisition, input-dependent problem organization could improve held-out surface transfer beyond fixed-layout computation and static transport under matched learning opportunities. EXP-0004 was inconclusive; EXP-0005 did not confirm reliable baseline acquisition. A further test requires a new protocol and queue decision.
hypotheses.falsifier: The benefit is explained by unequal designer-provided encodings or supervision, label leakage, unlimited representation search, or increased solver capacity without representation transfer.
